forces.title: Infrastructure scope expanding to include social assets
forces.description: The European infrastructure asset class is undergoing a structural change, with its scope broadening to encompass social infrastructure. This includes assets like radiology chains, nurseries, care homes, higher education facilities, and student accommodation. This shift provides new investment avenues and growth opportunities within the sector, driven by evolving societal needs and investor interest.
forces.source_title: European infrastructure is evolving—and investors are, too

forces.title: Demographic shifts boost demand for social healthcare infrastructure
forces.description: Europe's demographic shifts, particularly an ageing population, are creating a projected financing gap for healthcare systems. This trend necessitates additional acute and subacute care infrastructure and nursing homes, directly boosting demand for social infrastructure assets. Private capital is increasingly stepping in to meet this growing need, compensating for public budget strain.
forces.source_title: European infrastructure is evolving—and investors are, too

forces.title: Strained returns and dry powder slow infrastructure capital deployment
forces.description: Despite high investor interest, the European infrastructure sector faces challenges from strained returns and significant levels of dry powder. This has led to a slowdown in capital deployment in recent years, with investments in Europe dropping by about 40% from 2022 to 2024. This poses a key risk to funding new infrastructure projects, including social infrastructure, due to a mismatch between fundraising and deployment pace.
forces.source_title: European infrastructure is evolving—and investors are, too

forces.title: Public investments drive growth in social infrastructure buildings
forces.description: Public investments are providing a positive counterforce in the non-residential construction sector, specifically supporting healthcare and educational buildings across the EU. This trend indicates sustained government support and funding for the development and maintenance of social infrastructure assets, contributing to sector growth despite broader economic uncertainties and encouraging modernization.
forces.source_title: Construction Outlook 2026: Growth returns to the European construction sector

forces.title: Low government spending creates Greek housing affordability crisis
forces.description: Historically low central government spending on housing in Greece, coupled with the abolition of the Workers’ Housing Organization (OEK) in 2012, has severely undermined housing affordability for households. This policy gap has exacerbated a pressing social issue, leaving many Greeks dedicating an excessive share of income to housing, posing a significant headwind to urban social welfare and stability.
forces.source_title: Housing in Greece: Trends, challenges, and prospects

forces.title: Rising costs exacerbate Greece's housing affordability challenges
forces.description: Increasing energy costs and higher borrowing costs are further intensifying the housing affordability problem in Greece. These economic pressures, combined with low government support and a tight rental market due to tourism, make housing increasingly inaccessible for a growing share of the population, presenting a critical risk to urban social stability and household financial well-being.
forces.source_title: Housing in Greece: Trends, challenges, and prospects

forces.title: Irish government funding supports nursing home facility upgrades
forces.description: The Irish government's 2025 Residential Premises Upgrade (RPU) Scheme, with a €10 million allocation, aims to help nursing home operators upgrade facilities. This initiative, which supports converting multi-occupancy bedrooms to private en-suite rooms, directly promotes compliance with HIQA standards and enhances resident comfort, acting as a tailwind for social infrastructure development in elder care by improving existing assets.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025

forces.title: High costs hinder new Irish nursing home developments
forces.description: Feedback on Ireland's Design Guide for Long-Term Residential Care highlights "prohibitive costs" associated with implementing new design specifications. Respondents warned that without increased funding, developers might be reluctant to acquire sites and initiate planning, potentially leading to a decrease in new nursing home developments, posing a significant headwind to future social infrastructure expansion in elder care provision.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025

forces.title: Infrastructural bottlenecks impede Ireland's housing and development
forces.description: Ireland's economy is experiencing increasing infrastructural bottlenecks and capacity pressures, particularly in housing. Delays in delivering the National Development Plan and persistent planning issues are hindering progress. This represents a significant key risk, potentially preventing timely addressing of urban development and social infrastructure needs across the country, impacting overall economic stability and social welfare.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sector Insights & Outlook February 2025

forces.title: Inflated housing starts distort Ireland's 2025 completion forecasts
forces.description: Housing starts in Ireland during 2024 were artificially inflated as developers expedited projects to benefit from waivers on local authority and water infrastructure charges. This surge is expected to lead to house completions in 2025 falling below forecasts, indicating a cyclical fluctuation in urban housing supply driven by specific policy incentives rather than organic demand, creating market volatility.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sector Insights & Outlook February 2025

viewpoints.title: European infrastructure enters maturity, expanding to social assets, positive outlook
viewpoints.description: McKinsey reports European infrastructure is coming of age, with its scope broadening to include social assets like radiology chains and nurseries. LP sentiment remains very positive, with around half of LPs planning increased infrastructure allocations. This reflects growth in AUM from €91 billion in 2014 to €487 billion in 2025, suggesting a robust long-term outlook for the expanded asset class, including social infrastructure.
viewpoints.source_title: European infrastructure is evolving—and investors are, too

viewpoints.title: Greece's affordable housing faces significant challenges from policy and costs
viewpoints.description: The Institute of Economic and Industrial Research (IOBE) indicates that housing affordability in Greece has become a pressing social issue. Historically low central government spending on housing, the abolition of the Workers’ Housing Organization (OEK), and increasing energy and borrowing costs are exacerbating the problem. This points to a negative outlook for accessible housing provision and urban social welfare.
viewpoints.source_title: Housing in Greece: Trends, challenges, and prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish healthcare sector shows confidence with new projects and modernization
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland reports a positive outlook for the Irish healthcare sector, anticipating growth driven by new projects and modernization programs. This confidence extends to facilities such as day care centers, disability care services, and nursing homes, reflecting evolving care models and ongoing investment. The sector's resilience is underpinned by strong underlying needs from an aging population and increasing chronic illness.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Healthcare H1 2025 Insights / H2 2025 Outlook September 2025

viewpoints.title: Ireland's health sector outlook cautious positive with private and public efforts
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland maintains a cautious positive outlook for the Irish health sector in 2025. Despite ongoing challenges like workforce shortages and rising costs, the sector sees opportunities due to significant reliance on the private sector to address capacity shortfalls. Government initiatives like the Programme for Government and Sláintecare, focusing on infrastructure, also contribute to this optimism, signaling continued investment.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Health Insights 2024 / Outlook 2025 February 2025

viewpoints.title: Irish government committed to addressing housing supply and homelessness
viewpoints.description: Teagasc references the Irish government's "Delivering Homes, Building Communities 2025-2030: An Action Plan on Housing Supply and Targeting Homelessness." This action plan signals a strong commitment from the government to tackle critical urban development issues, aiming to increase housing supply and address homelessness. Such policy focus indicates sustained attention and investment in urban social infrastructure needs.
viewpoints.source_title: Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture 2026

new_opportunities.description: Day care services and the disability sector are emerging as growth areas for private operators, offering more flexible options for families and easing pressure on residential capacity, reflecting an unmet need.
